**Observation Log:**

[TEMPORAL] Session Date: 2023/08/15 (Tue) 12:11  
[FACT] User has a cable internet connection with Comcast.  
[FACT] User's current internet speed is supposed to be 150 Mbps.  
[FACT] User has multiple devices connected to their Wi-Fi network, including a smart TV, laptop, wireless speaker system, and a few smartphones.  
[FACT] User is experiencing slow speeds and dropped connections, especially in the evenings.  
[FACT] User has not changed anything in their home or network setup recently.  
[FACT] User has a lot of walls and furniture between their router and devices.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant offered to help troubleshoot the internet connection and improve Wi-Fi signal.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant requested information about the type of internet connection, ISP, current internet speed, connected devices, specific issues, recent changes in setup, and physical obstructions.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided general tips for troubleshooting, including restarting the router, checking for firmware updates, optimizing router placement, using a Wi-Fi analyzer app, changing the Wi-Fi channel, updating device Wi-Fi drivers, and considering a mesh network system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant suggested checking the router's location and surroundings, upgrading firmware, changing the Wi-Fi channel, using Quality of Service (QoS) settings, upgrading the router, reducing interference from other devices, checking for physical obstructions, monitoring network usage, and considering a mesh network system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant recommended specific mesh network systems compatible with Comcast: Netgear Orbi, Linksys Velop, Google Wifi, TP-Link Deco, and Comcast xFi.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant mentioned that all recommended mesh network systems support smart home devices.  
[USER] User expressed interest in the Google Wifi system.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided details about Google Wifi features, including tri-band Wi-Fi, mesh network capabilities, Network Assist technology, traffic prioritization, Google Wifi app management, and built-in security features.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant explained that Google Wifi can handle up to 150 devices per node and up to 900 devices total with multiple nodes.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant described Google Wifi's traffic prioritization feature as "Quality of Service" (QoS) and explained how it allows prioritization of certain devices or applications.
